A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SymmCD research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and rendered figures, support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MP-20 generation experiments, computational-efficiency measurements and a formation-energy prediction ablation.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds repeated-seed evaluations, MPTS-52 generation experiments and DFT relaxation analyses.

M1.justification: The symmetry representation, joint diffusion processes, losses, denoising network, projection and replication procedures remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 and Appendices A–E describe the same method; the added dataset experiments do not introduce a new component.

E1.justification: v2 adds training and evaluation on MPTS-52 alongside MP-20 (Section 5.6 and Appendix F.1). This extends coverage to crystals with up to 52 rather than 20 atoms per primitive cell and broader chemistry, including materials containing radioactive elements.

E2.justification: The evaluated generation baselines remain CDVAE, DiffCSP, DiffCSP++ and FlowMM. The new DFT comparison reuses this set, while MPTS-52 reports SymmCD alone. The original representation and property-prediction comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Stability evaluation expands from a random 1,000-crystal subset in v1 to all 10,000 generated crystals per method in v2. New protocols include CP2K relaxation of 100 structures per model and MPTS-52 training for 1,500 epochs with chronological train/validation/test splits. The original MP-20 split and preprocessing remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix F.6 add substantial physical-fidelity diagnostics through DFT relaxation displacements, residual gradients and nonconvergence analysis. Appendix F.2 extends atom-count distribution validation to MPTS-52. The original site-symmetry property-prediction ablation and six crystal examples are retained.

E5.justification: v2 first reports five seeded model trainings per method, with 10,000 generated samples per seed, and adds +/- variability to the main proxy-results table. v1 reports point values without run counts or uncertainty. This establishes expanded statistical reporting, although v1's run count and the precise meaning of v2's +/- statistic are unspecified.

E6.justification: Proxy scores are replaced by five-seed summaries, and stability results change under expanded sampling. v1 Table 3 reports 10-SG SymmCD S.U.N. yield of 9.9% versus DiffCSP's 9.7%; v2 Table 2 reports 7.59% versus 8.92% on 10,000 samples. These are revised evaluation summaries, not demonstrated same-setting performance changes. MPTS-52 and DFT results are added; original template, efficiency and regression-ablation values are retained.

T1.justification: The crystallographic definitions, replication construction, lattice constraints and diffusion equations remain substantively unchanged. No new theorem, proof or formal derivation is introduced; the new DFT quantities serve as empirical diagnostics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the central claims of symmetry-preserving generation, information sharing across space groups, structural diversity, competitive stability and computational efficiency. The additional experiments support these existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the earlier novelty-filtering advantage interpretation with a more qualified stability comparison. It acknowledges weaker structural validity, suggests limited access to interatomic distances as a cause, and discusses seed variability. The new DFT interpretation includes strong fidelity claims alongside substantive caveats about lax thresholds and roughly 60% nonconvergence. Existing composition-conditioning and polycrystal limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds extensive CP2K configuration details, including the functional, basis, pseudopotential, optimization settings and convergence thresholds. It also documents MPTS-52 splits and training duration, baseline retraining, and proxy evaluation on 1,000 valid crystals using a pretrained DimeNet++ energy predictor. These expand reproducibility information; the original model hyperparameters and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for MPTS-52, CP2K, PBE and EGNN, and notes the absence of reported de novo MPTS-52 results for its baselines. The central positioning against template-based DiffCSP++ and Wyckoff-label approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative places stability before proxy metrics, moves detailed proxy definitions into Appendix F.5 and reorganizes Appendix F around the extensions. Elsewhere, revisions mainly shorten wording, standardize terminology and rename algorithm headings. The main exposition and method structure remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds MPTS-52 distribution plots and result tables, DFT displacement and gradient plots, and configuration and gradient-summary tables. It also uses denser formatting for the proxy-results table and relocates several displays. The original atom-count histogram, property ablation and crystal examples remain identifiable despite renumbering and presentation changes.

improvement.justification: Five-seed proxy comparisons and the larger stability evaluation substantially strengthen empirical reliability and temper the earlier S.U.N. superiority interpretation. MPTS-52 supplies direct evidence for larger-crystal applicability, with expanded reproducibility documentation. These gains outweigh weaknesses in the new DFT superiority evidence: most relaxations fail to converge, and Table 10's reported mean gradients appear inconsistent with Figure 10's distribution.
